question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` expose internal OpenClaw tool-call telemetry, and if so what redaction, scope, and opt-in contract should protect it?
rationale: Current source and release docs intentionally define a client-tool contract, while the requested internal telemetry would cross a full-operator HTTP security boundary and may expose sensitive tool arguments or results.

options.title: Keep the current contract
options.body: Leave Chat Completions `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied HTTP tools and point internal-tool visibility to existing audit, plugin hook, Gateway Protocol, or future diagnostic surfaces.

options.title: Design an opt-in diagnostic mode
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved redacted telemetry mode or header only after specifying scopes, redaction, compatibility, and tests for streaming and non-streaming responses.

options.title: Move visibility outside Chat Completions
options.body: Treat internal tool visibility as a plugin, OpenResponses, or Gateway Protocol feature instead of extending the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions response shape.

recommendation.title: Keep the current contract
recommendation.body: Leave Chat Completions `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied HTTP tools and point internal-tool visibility to existing audit, plugin hook, Gateway Protocol, or future diagnostic surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Gateway HTTP product contract and security posture, and steipete merged the relevant client-tool protocol PRs and follow-up contract changes.
